text:
alex_w: Heads-up — prepping a hardening checklist for a new private deployment (customer-managed VPC + on-prem gateway). Need quick sign-off on RBAC changes, KMS integration tests, audit log retention, and an egress verification plan. Who can help pull a minimal safe baseline?
sec-bot: Automated compliance scan scheduled for 1967890500. Posting current control gaps after run. :gear:

maria_p: Start with least-privilege RBAC. Remove cluster-admin from service accounts and use narrowly scoped roles. Example pattern: create a read-only SA + role for metrics ingestion.
```bash
# example: bind prometheus to read-only on monitoring namespace
kubectl create role prometheus-read 
  --verb=get,list,watch 
  --resource=pods,services,endpoints 
  -n monitoring
kubectl create rolebinding prometheus-read-binding 
  --role=prometheus-read 
  --serviceaccount=monitoring:prometheus
  -n monitoring
```

samir: On network isolation: default deny all egress, allow only: customer KMS endpoints, logging backhaul (syslog/s3), attestation/metadata endpoints if needed. Prefer cloud-native NetPolicy + host-level iptables for extra defense.
```yaml
# minimal example netpol: deny egress except to logging and kms
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-except-allowlist
  namespace: default
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.1.2.0/24 # logging host subnet
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 3.5.6.0/24 # kms egress prefix (example)
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

ingrid: Audit logging: centralize to retained, immutable store. Compliance asks for 1 year retention for auth/privilege changes and 3 years for sensitive access events. All logs must be encrypted at rest — rewrapped with the deployment KMS.

maria_p: KMS integration notes: use envelope encryption (data keys encrypted by customer-managed CMK). Test plans: create a test key, rotate, and run rewrap on a small dataset. If key compromise suspected, steps: 1) revoke grants, 2) create replacement CMK 3) re-encrypt data keys and update configs. Sample AWS flow (example):
```bash
# create key (example)
aws kms create-key --description "redwood-private-deploy-cmk"
# re-encrypt data key with new CMK
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://encrypted-data-key.blob --destination-key-id <new-key-id>
# schedule old key disable -> deletion after verification
aws kms schedule-key-deletion --key-id <old-key-id> --pending-window-in-days 30
```
Note: verify key policies allow only specific service principals and an emergency IAM role.

ops_oncall: Incident playbook additions: if exfiltration/KMS misuse suspected -> isolate affected nodes (cordon + drain to preserve forensic), revoke KMS grants, rotate CMK, preserve logs (write-once backup), raise IRP pager, and notify legal/compliance. Keep one immutable forensic image.

samir: Egress verification plan (quick tests): 1) tcpdump on egress gateway for 24h sample, 2) run synthetic outbound attempts to disallowed hosts (should fail), 3) attempt SSRF to metadata endpoints from app pods (must be blocked). Example test commands:
```bash
# from pod: should be blocked
curl -sv http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data || echo "blocked"
# attempt to reach disallowed external host (should timeout/connrefused)
curl -sv http://8.8.8.8 || echo "blocked"
```

maria_p: Quick checklist to add to playbook (owner tags):
- RBAC: remove cluster-admin, create scoped SAs (owner: infra)
- KMS: envelope encryption, test rewrap & rotation (owner: security)
- Audit: central encrypted store, 365d retention for auth events (owner: observability)
- Network: default deny egress, ips/hosts allowlist, verify with synthetic tests (owner: netops)
- IR: revoke grants + rotate keys + preserve forensic snapshot (owner: oncall)

alex_w: This is great — please add to /repos/playbooks/security/private-deploy-hardening.md and ping me when owners are assigned. I'll fold into the customer onboarding checklist. :thumbsup:
